title: Thesis submitted: wear, friction and a lot of thanks

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: After about three years, a master's thesis is in. Antoine has submitted his at ÉTS.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Congratulations to him. What was it about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Real-time simulation of surface wear. It sits where physical simulation, contact and graphics rendering meet. The topic on his CV is real-time surface wear in interactive physics simulations, with dynamic friction and textures.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wear as in things getting scuffed and worn down?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea. And the post ties it to the rest of his work. The contact model is friction that depends on direction and on the material pair, the same thread as his pull requests to IPC Toolkit. Another project, TrueMapData, reads height maps that describe real worn surfaces. And a third, MistubaVideo, turns recorded poses and surface fields into frames and video.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the thesis is the center of a few tools.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pretty much. The work was also presented at GraphQuon in 2024 and 2025.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sheldon Andrews supervised the thesis. Seven other people are named for advice and help along the way, including Paul Kry and Mélissa Katz.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, a write-up on wear in texture space is coming soon. For now there's a thesis article with the current project overview. This post is the short announcement, and it links out to all of those.
